lead:
A court ordered the downstream regulator to keep licensing three big marketers to import petrol, the government sought $1.5 billion in new World Bank credit, and Omoyele Sowore's party went to court over the President's month-long absence.

The day in brief: Justice Inyang Ekwo held that the NMDPRA's refusal to license Matrix Energy, AA Rano and AYM Shafa breached the Petroleum Industry Act. World Bank papers showed the new financing is three $500 million credits for social protection, early childhood and climate resilience, and Atiku Abubakar said past loans must be accounted for first. The AAC asked the Federal High Court to declare that Tinubu broke the Constitution by not handing power to Kashim Shettima before his vacation. Kenya's William Ruto called the Dangote refinery a masterpiece as the group forecast $36 billion in revenue for the year. GTCO's half-year pre-tax profit edged up to N603 billion, JAMB restored its admissions portal, and ASUU suspended its strike at Ondo state universities. In Plateau, gunmen killed three women at a mining site in Barkin Ladi.

items.h: Court orders NMDPRA to keep granting import licences to AA Rano and others
items.s: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja ordered the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority to “continue to grant” petrol import licences to Matrix Energy, AA Rano and AYM Shafa in line with the law. In Monday's judgment he held that the regulator's refusal to issue licences to the three marketers was in direct breach of the Petroleum Industry Act.

items.h: FG seeks $1.5bn World Bank loan; Atiku demands accounting
items.s: World Bank documents show the government is seeking three separate $500 million International Development Association credits to widen social protection, improve early childhood development and scale up climate resilience, as public debt reaches N166.79 trillion. Atiku Abubakar accused the government of demanding endless sacrifice from Nigerians while borrowing without end, and said it must first explain how earlier loans were spent.

items.h: AAC sues over Tinubu's failure to transfer power to Shettima
items.s: The African Action Congress filed an originating summons at the Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday asking it to declare that President Tinubu's failure to send a letter transferring power to Vice President Shettima before his European trip, from 30 August to 28 September, was “undemocratic and a gross violation of the Constitution.” The suit was filed by the party's legal adviser, Inibehe Effiong.

items.h: Ruto tours Dangote refinery as group targets $36bn revenue
items.s: Kenya's President William Ruto, stopping in Lagos after the UN General Assembly, toured the 700,000-barrel-a-day Dangote refinery and called it “a masterpiece of science, engineering and art.” Dangote Group's chief strategy officer, Aliyu Suleiman, said revenue reached about $17 billion in the first half of 2026 and that the group expects to double last year's $18 billion to $36 billion this year.

items.h: GTCO half-year pre-tax profit reaches N603bn
items.s: GTCO's audited half-year accounts show profit before tax of N603.03 billion, a 0.35 per cent rise from N600.90 billion a year earlier, with gross earnings up 3.25 per cent to N1.11 trillion. Interest and trading income grew strongly, but a N46.2 billion fair-value loss held back profit, and earnings per share fell to N11.18. The board proposed an interim dividend of N1 a share.

items.h: Gunmen kill three women at Plateau mining site
items.s: Gunmen stormed a mining site at Rakum in Barkin Ladi, Plateau State, at about 4.30pm on Monday and opened fire on the workers, killing three women and injuring another person. The attack came amid heightened tension after dozens of farmers and herders were reportedly killed in separate attacks in Mangu, Barkin Ladi and Bokkos, where the state government imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew.

items.h: Court sets 13 October hearing on Atiku's motion to amend Tinubu suit
items.s: Justice Inyang Ekwo fixed 13 October to hear a motion by Atiku Abubakar and the ADC to amend their suit challenging President Tinubu's eligibility to contest in 2027, after confirming that the respondents had been served. The APC and INEC are also defendants in the case, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026.

items.h: Troops arrest suspected ransom couriers and rescue 14 in Katsina
items.s: Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma said they intercepted suspected ransom couriers in Faskari, Katsina, seizing N2.7 million believed to be ransom money, and rescued 14 kidnap victims. In neighbouring Zamfara the same operation said it foiled two abduction attempts in Maru and freed 10 villagers, while in Sokoto's Gudu area soldiers raided a camp, killed a suspected terrorist and recovered weapons.

items.h: Tinubu says credit guarantees unlocked N46.95bn in loans
items.s: President Tinubu said on X that the National Credit Guarantee Company, working through 19 lenders, helped unlock N46.95 billion in loans in its first year by issuing N21.59 billion in guarantees, meaning lenders extended about N2.17 for every naira guaranteed. He said 67,512 borrowers in 25 states and the FCT benefited, including 11,374 women, and that a third were first-time formal borrowers.

items.h: FG targets one million outsourcing jobs by 2030
items.s: At the New York launch of a “Hire From Nigeria” campaign during the UN General Assembly, the government set a goal of one million export-linked jobs and 10 million globally certified Nigerians by 2030, aiming to win a bigger share of the world's outsourcing and digital services market. Vice President Shettima's address was delivered by deputy chief of staff Ibrahim Hadejia, and Education Minister Tunji Alausa also spoke.

items.h: Shettima returns from UNGA after pressing Africa's case
items.s: Vice President Kashim Shettima returned from the 81st UN General Assembly, where he restated Africa's demand for permanent seats on the Security Council. In a meeting with the UN Deputy Secretary-General he said Africa's exclusion undermines the fairness and legitimacy of global governance, and that Nigeria would remain a dependable partner in reforming the UN and defending international law.

items.h: JAMB restores CAPS and urges faster admissions
items.s: JAMB said its Central Admissions Processing System is fully working again after a temporary disruption, and told universities, polytechnics and colleges to speed up 2026/2027 admissions and make up the time lost so they meet the agreed deadlines. It also advised candidates to accept offers made to them on the system promptly.

items.h: ASUU suspends strike at Ondo state universities
items.s: ASUU suspended its weeks-long strike in Ondo State-owned universities after the state government made financial interventions, said Boluwaji Oshodi, chairman of the union at Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko. But the chapter at the University of Medical Sciences, Ondo, rejected the deal, saying it was not invited to the talks and that its members remain on strike.

items.h: UBEC to begin 10-year basic education roadmap in October
items.s: UBEC will begin its 10-year Universal Basic Education roadmap, 2026 to 2035, in the first week of October, executive secretary Aisha Garba said at a workshop with SUBEB chairmen. The plan moves away from one-off projects such as building classrooms or supplying furniture towards assessing all of a school's needs, and a new digital system will be used to plan and monitor intervention funds.

items.h: Atiku backs labour's call for higher minimum wage
items.s: Atiku Abubakar backed organised labour's demand for a substantial rise in the minimum wage, saying the increase from N30,000 to N70,000 had not restored workers' purchasing power. He accused the government of a “ruthless economic squeeze” in which workers are paid more on paper but live on less, with wages that vanish between the filling station and the food market.

items.h: Melaye says ADC would cut petrol to N400
items.s: Dino Melaye, an ADC chieftain, defended the party's plan to restore petrol subsidy, saying it would cut the pump price from about N1,400 a litre to between N400 and N500 and bring down the cost of goods and services. He spoke on AIT's Democracy Today programme on Monday, arguing the policy is meant to make Nigeria affordable for ordinary citizens.

items.h: APM demands Okpebholo resign over fuel price remark
items.s: The Allied Peoples Movement called on Edo Governor Monday Okpebholo to resign after he was reported to have justified the rising price of petrol by comparing it with prices in the United Kingdom. The party said the remark showed insensitivity to the hardship Nigerians face, rejected the current price of over N1,500 a litre, and warned the federal government against further increases.

items.h: Kano governor says Tinubu must complete South's eight years
items.s: Kano Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf urged Nigerians to re-elect President Tinubu in 2027 so the South can complete an eight-year turn before power returns to the North. He spoke at Government House, Kano, while unveiling 50 vehicles donated by Government Ekpemupolo, known as Tompolo, for the APC's campaign mobilisation in the state.

items.h: Makinde promises to reset Nigeria in four years
items.s: Seyi Makinde, Oyo's governor and the APM's presidential candidate, told a North Central town hall in Lafia that he could reset Nigeria within four years if elected in 2027. “I'm a resetter, are you a resetter? Together, we shall reset this country,” he told supporters, who included market women, women farmers and widows, and he thanked Governor Abdullahi Sule for hosting his team.

items.h: NDC North-East candidates reject Babachir Lawal's appointment
items.s: Six governorship candidates of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in the North-East wrote to the party's national leader, Seriake Dickson, rejecting the appointment of former SGF Babachir Lawal as the party's leader in the zone. They called their decision “collective, firm and final.” Lawal was named only days after joining the party, exposing friction between local stalwarts and new arrivals.

items.h: Imo APC calls Wike a threat to democracy
items.s: The APC in Imo State described FCT Minister Nyesom Wike as a threat to Nigeria's democracy, deepening the rift between Wike and APC governors over his Rainbow Coalition's campaign for President Tinubu's re-election. Wike's media aide, Lere Olayinka, and the Imo PDP hit back, saying it is the APC that endangers democracy.

items.h: INEC, APC and Yahaya Bello ask court to dismiss senatorial ticket suit
items.s: INEC, the APC and former Kogi governor Yahaya Bello asked the court to throw out a suit by an aspirant, Mr Obaro, who claims he won the party's 18 May primary for a Kogi senatorial seat. In the case filed on 29 May he wants the court to declare that, having scored the most lawful votes, his name should be forwarded to INEC as the APC candidate.

items.h: DSS secures death sentence over Sokoto kidnap killings
items.s: The DSS secured the conviction and death sentence of Ibrahim Usman, known as Dan Iyali, at the Sokoto High Court for his role in the kidnapping and killing of three people in Sokoto State in September 2023. He was tried on four counts, including conspiracy, kidnapping and culpable homicide, alongside other suspects who remain at large.

items.h: DSS arraigns four over killing of operative
items.s: The DSS arraigned four suspected members of the proscribed IPOB, Michael Okafor, Chinedu Joseph Chukwudozie, Chibunna Olisa and Chigozie Olisa, before the Federal High Court in Abuja on a six-count charge of terrorism and the kidnapping and killing of its officer, Ekpeyong Asuquo Owoh.

items.h: NDLEA destroys cannabis farms in Edo
items.s: NDLEA officers and soldiers destroyed two cannabis plantations covering about half a hectare at Eko Camp, Illushi, in Esan South East, Edo State, estimated to hold 1,360kg of the drug, and recovered 107kg of processed cannabis and seeds. Two men were arrested in the operation on 23 September, state commander Mitchell Ofoyeju told journalists in Benin.

items.h: Fire hits Customs Western Marine Command office in Apapa
items.s: Fire broke out at about 10.23am on Monday in the conference room of the Nigeria Customs Service's Western Marine Command office in Apapa, Lagos, after an electrical surge, and spread to other parts of the building, destroying property worth millions of naira. Officers on duty fought the blaze until the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service arrived about 20 minutes later.

items.h: Reps panel writes CBN over audited accounts
items.s: The House of Representatives Committee on Delegated Legislation wrote to the CBN, special investigator Jim Obazee, the Financial Reporting Council and the audit firms KPMG and EY over alleged irregularities in the central bank's 2024 and 2025 audited accounts. In letters dated 22 September and signed by chairman Olufemi Bamisile, it asked the CBN to submit its consolidated financial statements for both years.

items.h: Court to rule on halting inquest into Adichie's son's death
items.s: Justice Aishat Opesanwo of the Lagos High Court in Ikoyi will rule on 12 October on whether to halt the coroner's inquest into the death of Nkanu, son of author Chimamanda Adichie and Dr Ivara Esege, who died during procedures at Euracare hospital. The parents, through Kemi Pinheiro SAN, said the hospital operator's application was premature because the coroner had not yet decided anything.

items.h: Ground handlers to stop serving XEJet over N300m debt
items.s: The Aviation Ground Handlers Association of Nigeria told its members to withdraw all services from XEJet Airlines immediately over unpaid bills of about N300 million, saying the airline failed to keep agreed payment plans. The withdrawal on Monday disrupted the carrier's luggage handling and ramp support, and some of its flights were diverted.

items.h: FAAN car age deadline threatens 300 airport taxi jobs
items.s: About 300 airport taxi and car-hire workers could lose their jobs as FAAN enforces an October 2026 deadline for operators to replace vehicles made before 2012. Prince Amosola, chairman of the Airport Cab Operators, said the 17 licensed companies are struggling to meet the requirement and warned it could push hundreds of people into a crowded job market.

items.h: CBN warns Kano traders against mishandling naira
items.s: The CBN began a campaign in Kano markets, starting at Galadima Market, urging traders and residents to handle naira notes with care and treat the currency with dignity. Its currency operations department said careful handling extends the life of notes and cuts the cost of replacing soiled and mutilated ones.

items.h: Usor eyes more after Super Eagles debut
items.s: Ahead of Tuesday's 2027 AFCON qualifier, CAF appointed an all-Ethiopian refereeing team, with Tewodros Mitiku in the middle, for the 4pm kick-off in Bissau. Former international Sam Elijah warned the Super Eagles not to underrate Guinea-Bissau, who beat co-hosts Tanzania 2-0 in Zanzibar in their opener, and debutant Usor said he wanted to build on his first appearance.
